posts.title: Rowhammer Backdoor Injection Attack During Inference (Northeastern)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Northeastern University published a technical paper titled “ROBBIN: Rowhammer-Based Backdoor Injection during Inference.” Abstract excerpt: “This work presents ROBBIN, a hardware-aware Rowhammer-based backdoor injection attack that integrates the device-specific vulnerability into the backdoor construction process. ROBBIN first characterizes the bit-flip patterns of a target DRAM and uses this information to iteratively select DRAM... » read more
The post Rowhammer Backdoor Injection Attack During Inference (Northeastern) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Northeastern University researchers introduced 'ROBBIN,' a hardware-aware attack that leverages Rowhammer-induced bit-flips to inject backdoors into AI models during inference.
Unlike previous methods that treat bit-flips as side effects, ROBBIN characterizes specific DRAM vulnerabilities to strategically map model weights to susceptible memory pages.
This approach creates highly robust backdoors that maintain high attack success rates (ASR) while preserving the target accuracy (TA) of the model across different hardware devices.
The research underscores a critical security vulnerability in AI deployment, as it demonstrates that hardware-level memory manipulation can compromise model integrity even after deployment.

posts.title: Predicting Post-Route PPA from Macro and Standard-Cell Placements (U. of Alberta)
posts.summary:
Researchers from University of Alberta published a technical paper titled “PPAPlace: Differentiable Cross-Stage Objectives for Chip Placement Optimization.” Abstract: “Macro placement significantly affects a chip’s post-route performance, power, and area (PPA). Most placement methods optimize half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL) as the primary objective. However, recent benchmarking shows a near-zero correlation between HPWL and post-route timing metrics... » read more
The post Predicting Post-Route PPA from Macro and Standard-Cell Placements (U. of Alberta) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at the University of Alberta developed 'PPAPlace,' a differentiable surrogate model that predicts post-route timing metrics directly from macro and standard-cell placements.
The study highlights that traditional HPWL-based optimization correlates poorly with final timing, leading to PPA degradation in existing AI-driven placement tools.
By utilizing post-global-routing labels, the model achieved a 22% improvement in worst negative slack (WNS) and a 51% improvement in total negative slack (TNS) on benchmark circuits.
The PPAPlace framework integrates into existing analytical placers as a co-objective or a refinement step, offering a path to better silicon performance without requiring retraining for new circuits.

posts.title: FAW-VW opens ID. AURA T6 pre-sales, betting on locally developed smart tech to win over Chinese buyers
posts.summary:
The ID. AURA T6 starts at a pre-sales price of 135,900 yuan ($20,040) and offers a range of up to 660 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: FAW-Volkswagen has launched pre-sales for the ID. AURA T6, a mid-size electric SUV priced between 135,900 and 169,900 yuan, marking the debut of the new AURA lineup.

The vehicle is built on the CEA architecture, a joint development between Volkswagen and Xpeng, which utilizes a central computing and zonal control design to support advanced OTA updates and AI model deployment.
The high-end variants feature 192-channel LiDAR and an intelligent driving system powered by Horizon Robotics' Journey 6H chip, delivering 420 TOPS of computing power for urban NOA capabilities.
This launch signifies a strategic shift for Volkswagen, as it increasingly integrates Chinese technology partners to compete with local smart EV brands in the mid-market segment.

posts.title: Xpeng Q2 revenue rises 8% as net loss nearly triples
posts.summary:
Xpeng's second-quarter revenue reached 19.74 billion yuan, while its gross margin rose to 20.7%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xpeng reported a 179% year-on-year surge in net loss to 1.34 billion yuan, despite an 8% increase in quarterly revenue to 19.74 billion yuan.
Gross margin improved to 20.7%, bolstered significantly by technical R&D services provided to Volkswagen and increased parts sales.
Vehicle margin remained flat at 12.1% sequentially, as the company navigates a transition between vehicle product generations.
Rising R&D expenditures, up 32.1% year-on-year, highlight the company's aggressive investment in AI-related technologies and new model development.

posts.title: Wall Street sees Xpeng robot financing as catalyst for value unlock
posts.summary:
Several Wall Street banks believe that external capital has established an independent valuation benchmark for Xpeng's robotics business.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xpeng's robotics unit, Dogotix, secured $900 million in financing, establishing an independent valuation of approximately $5 billion to $6.3 billion.
Wall Street analysts view the external funding as a positive catalyst that provides a clear valuation anchor, allowing investors to decouple the robotics business from Xpeng's core EV operations.
The participation of strategic investors like Alibaba and Tencent, alongside IDG Capital, is seen as a strong validation of Xpeng's integrated physical AI strategy.
